Each supervisory authority has corrective powers including issuing warnings and reprimands; ordering compliance with data-subject rights and GDPR requirements; ordering breach communication, rectification, erasure or restriction; imposing processing limitations or bans; withdrawing or requiring withdrawal of certifications; imposing administrative fines under Article 83; and ordering suspension of data flows to third countries or international organisations.

Each supervisory authority has authorisation and advisory powers including advising controllers during prior consultation; issuing opinions to public bodies and the public; authorising processing where Member State law requires it; approving codes of conduct and certification criteria; accrediting certification bodies; issuing certifications; adopting or authorising standard clauses and administrative arrangements; and approving binding corporate rules.

The exercise of supervisory authority powers under this Article must be subject to appropriate safeguards, including effective judicial remedy and due process, established by Union and Member State law in accordance with the Charter.

Each Member State must provide by law that its supervisory authority has the power to bring infringements of the Regulation to judicial authorities and, where appropriate, commence or otherwise participate in legal proceedings to enforce the Regulation.

Each Member State may provide by law for additional powers for its supervisory authority beyond those in paragraphs 1, 2 and 3, provided that exercising those powers does not impair the effective operation of Chapter VII.

Each supervisory authority shall draw up an annual report on its activities, which may include types of infringements notified and types of measures taken under Article 58(2). The reports shall be transmitted to the national parliament, government and other authorities designated by Member State law, and made available to the public, the Commission and the Board.

article_name: Cooperation between the lead supervisory authority and the other supervisory authorities concerned

sections.text: The lead supervisory authority shall cooperate with the other supervisory authorities concerned to seek consensus and shall exchange all relevant information with them.

The lead supervisory authority may request mutual assistance under Article 61 and conduct joint operations under Article 62 with other supervisory authorities, particularly for investigations or monitoring measures concerning a controller or processor established in another Member State.

The lead supervisory authority shall promptly communicate relevant information to the other supervisory authorities concerned, submit a draft decision for their opinion, and take due account of their views.

If a supervisory authority concerned raises a relevant and reasoned objection to the draft decision within four weeks, the lead supervisory authority shall submit the matter to the consistency mechanism under Article 63 if it does not follow the objection or considers it not relevant or reasoned.

Where the lead supervisory authority intends to follow a relevant and reasoned objection, it shall submit a revised draft decision to the other supervisory authorities concerned, which is subject to the procedure in paragraph 4 within two weeks.

If none of the other supervisory authorities concerned objects to the draft decision within the applicable period, the lead supervisory authority and the other supervisory authorities concerned are deemed to agree with and are bound by the draft decision.

The lead supervisory authority shall adopt and notify the decision to the main or single establishment of the controller or processor, inform the other supervisory authorities concerned and the Board, and provide a summary of the relevant facts and grounds. The supervisory authority receiving a complaint shall inform the complainant of the decision.

Where a complaint is dismissed or rejected, the supervisory authority with which the complaint was lodged shall, by derogation from paragraph 7, adopt the decision, notify it to the complainant and inform the controller.

Where parts of a complaint are dismissed or rejected and other parts are acted upon, separate decisions shall be adopted for each part. The lead supervisory authority shall decide the part concerning action against the controller and notify the relevant establishment and complainant, while the supervisory authority of the complainant shall decide the dismissed or rejected part and notify the complainant and controller or processor.

After notification of the decision, the controller or processor shall take the necessary measures to ensure compliance for processing activities across all its establishments in the Union and shall notify those measures to the lead supervisory authority, which shall inform the other supervisory authorities concerned.

Where, in exceptional circumstances, a supervisory authority concerned considers that urgent action is necessary to protect the interests of data subjects, the urgency procedure under Article 66 shall apply.
The lead supervisory authority and the other supervisory authorities concerned shall provide each other with the information required under this Article electronically using a standardised format.

Supervisory authorities shall exchange relevant information and provide mutual assistance to ensure consistent implementation and application of the Regulation, including information requests and supervisory measures such as prior authorisations and consultations, inspections and investigations.

Each supervisory authority shall take appropriate measures to respond to another supervisory authority's request without undue delay and no later than one month after receiving it, including, where appropriate, transmitting relevant information concerning an investigation.
Requests for assistance shall contain all necessary information, including their purpose and reasons. Information exchanged may be used only for the purpose for which it was requested.

A requested supervisory authority may refuse a request only where it lacks competence for the subject matter or requested measures, or where complying would infringe the Regulation or applicable Union or Member State law.

The requested supervisory authority shall inform the requesting authority of the results or progress of measures taken in response to the request and shall give reasons for any refusal under paragraph 4.
Requested supervisory authorities shall, as a rule, provide requested information electronically using a standardised format.

Requested supervisory authorities shall not charge a fee for actions taken in response to mutual assistance requests. Supervisory authorities may agree on rules for indemnifying each other for specific expenditure arising from mutual assistance in exceptional circumstances.

If a supervisory authority does not provide the information required under paragraph 5 within one month, the requesting authority may adopt a provisional measure in its Member State under Article 55(1). In such circumstances, the urgent need to act under Article 66(1) is presumed and requires an urgent binding decision from the Board under Article 66(2).

The Commission may specify, by implementing acts, the format and procedures for mutual assistance and electronic information exchange between supervisory authorities and between supervisory authorities and the Board, including the standardised format referred to in paragraph 6. Such implementing acts shall follow the examination procedure under Article 93(2).

Supervisory authorities shall, where appropriate, conduct joint operations, including joint investigations and joint enforcement measures involving members or staff of supervisory authorities from other Member States.

Where a controller or processor has establishments in several Member States, or processing is likely to substantially affect a significant number of data subjects in more than one Member State, the supervisory authorities of those Member States have the right to participate in joint operations. The authority competent under Article 56(1) or (4) shall invite them to participate and respond without delay to participation requests.

A supervisory authority may, in accordance with Member State law and with the seconding authority's authorisation, confer investigative or other powers on participating members or staff, or permit them to exercise investigative powers under the seconding Member State's law where the host Member State permits it. Such powers may be exercised only under the host authority's guidance and presence, and participating staff are subject to the host Member State's law.

Where staff of a seconding supervisory authority operate in another Member State, the host Member State assumes responsibility for their actions, including liability for damage caused during their operations, in accordance with the law of the Member State where they operate.

The Member State where damage was caused shall compensate the damage under the conditions applicable to damage caused by its own staff. The Member State of the seconding supervisory authority whose staff caused damage shall fully reimburse the other Member State for amounts it paid to entitled persons.

Except as provided in paragraph 5 and without prejudice to rights against third parties, each Member State shall refrain from seeking reimbursement from another Member State for damage referred to in paragraph 4.

Where a joint operation is intended and a supervisory authority fails within one month to comply with its obligation under the second sentence of paragraph 2, the other supervisory authorities may adopt a provisional measure in their Member State under Article 55. The urgent need to act under Article 66(1) is then presumed and requires an opinion or urgent binding decision from the Board under Article 66(2).

The supervisory authorities shall cooperate with each other and, where relevant, with the Commission through the consistency mechanism established in this Section to contribute to the consistent application of the Regulation throughout the Union.

The Board shall issue an opinion when a competent supervisory authority intends to adopt specified measures, including lists of processing operations requiring a data protection impact assessment, opinions or approvals concerning codes of conduct, accreditation requirements and certification criteria, standard data protection clauses, certain contractual clauses, or binding corporate rules. The competent supervisory authority shall communicate the draft decision to the Board.

Any supervisory authority, the Chair of the Board or the Commission may request the Board to examine a matter of general application or producing effects in more than one Member State, particularly where a competent supervisory authority does not comply with obligations concerning mutual assistance under Article 61 or joint operations under Article 62.

The Board shall issue an opinion on matters submitted under paragraphs 1 and 2 where it has not already issued an opinion on the same matter. The opinion shall normally be adopted within eight weeks by simple majority, with a possible six-week extension due to complexity. A Board member who does not object within the period indicated by the Chair is deemed to agree with the draft decision.

Supervisory authorities and the Commission shall communicate relevant information to the Board without undue delay by electronic means using a standardised format, including, where applicable, a summary of facts, the draft decision, reasons for the proposed measure and the views of other supervisory authorities concerned.

The Chair of the Board shall without undue delay electronically inform the Board members and the Commission of relevant information received using the standardised format, with translations provided by the Board secretariat where necessary. The Chair shall also inform the relevant supervisory authority and the Commission of the opinion and make the opinion public.
The competent supervisory authority referred to in paragraph 1 shall not adopt its draft decision during the period specified for the Board's opinion under paragraph 3.

The competent supervisory authority shall take utmost account of the Board's opinion and, within two weeks of receiving it, electronically inform the Chair whether it will maintain or amend its draft decision and, where applicable, provide the amended draft decision using the standardised format.

Where the competent supervisory authority informs the Chair within the period referred to in paragraph 7 that it will not follow the Board's opinion, wholly or partly, and provides relevant grounds, Article 65(1) shall apply.

To ensure the correct and consistent application of the Regulation in individual cases, the Board shall adopt a binding decision where a relevant and reasoned objection to a lead supervisory authority's draft decision is not followed or is rejected; where supervisory authorities have conflicting views on which authority is competent for the main establishment; or where a competent supervisory authority fails to request or follow an opinion of the Board under Article 64. The decision shall address the matters covered by the relevant objection, including whether the Regulation has been infringed.

The Board shall adopt the binding decision within one month of referral by a two-thirds majority, with a possible one-month extension due to complexity. The reasoned decision shall be addressed to and binding on the lead supervisory authority and all supervisory authorities concerned.

If the Board cannot adopt a decision within the periods specified in paragraph 2, it shall adopt the decision within two weeks after the second month by simple majority. If the members are equally divided, the decision shall be adopted by the Chair's vote.
The supervisory authorities concerned shall not adopt a decision on the matter submitted to the Board under paragraph 1 during the periods specified in paragraphs 2 and 3.

The Chair of the Board shall notify the binding decision to the supervisory authorities concerned without undue delay and inform the Commission. The decision shall be published on the Board's website without delay after the relevant supervisory authority has notified its final decision under paragraph 6.

The lead supervisory authority or, where applicable, the supervisory authority with which the complaint was lodged shall adopt its final decision based on the Board's binding decision without undue delay and no later than one month after notification by the Board. It shall inform the Board when the final decision is notified to the controller or processor and data subject. The final decision shall follow Article 60(7), (8) and (9), refer to the Board's decision, state that it will be published on the Board's website, and attach the Board's decision.

In exceptional circumstances requiring urgent action to protect data subjects' rights and freedoms, a concerned supervisory authority may derogate from the consistency or cooperation procedures and immediately adopt provisional measures producing legal effects in its territory for a specified period not exceeding three months. It shall without delay communicate the measures and reasons to the other concerned supervisory authorities, the Board and the Commission.

Where a supervisory authority has adopted provisional measures under paragraph 1 and considers that final measures are urgently required, it may request an urgent opinion or urgent binding decision from the Board, stating the reasons for the request.

Any supervisory authority may request an urgent opinion or urgent binding decision from the Board where a competent supervisory authority has failed to take an appropriate measure despite an urgent need to protect data subjects' rights and freedoms. The request shall state the reasons, including the urgent need for action.

Urgent opinions or urgent binding decisions requested under paragraphs 2 and 3 shall be adopted by the Board within two weeks by simple majority, notwithstanding the time limits otherwise applicable under Articles 64(3) and 65(2).

The Commission may adopt implementing acts of general scope specifying arrangements for electronic exchange of information between supervisory authorities and between supervisory authorities and the Board, including the standardised format referred to in Article 64. Such implementing acts shall be adopted in accordance with the examination procedure under Article 93(2).
The European Data Protection Board is established as a body of the Union and has legal personality.
The Board shall be represented by its Chair.
The Board shall consist of the head of one supervisory authority from each Member State and the European Data Protection Supervisor, or their respective representatives.

Where more than one supervisory authority in a Member State is responsible for monitoring the application of the Regulation, that Member State shall appoint a joint representative in accordance with its law.
The Commission may participate in the Board's activities and meetings without voting rights and shall designate a representative. The Chair shall communicate the Board's activities to the Commission.

In cases under Article 65, the European Data Protection Supervisor shall have voting rights only for decisions concerning principles and rules applicable to Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies that correspond in substance to this Regulation.
The Board shall act independently when performing its tasks and exercising its powers under Articles 70 and 71.
Except for requests made by the Commission under Article 70(1) and (2), the Board shall neither seek nor take instructions from any person or body when performing its tasks or exercising its powers.

The Board shall ensure consistent application of the Regulation and, on its own initiative or where relevant at the Commission's request, perform specified tasks including monitoring application in consistency cases, advising the Commission, issuing guidelines, recommendations and best practices, supporting consistent approaches to profiling, breach notification, international transfers and enforcement, promoting codes of conduct and certification, issuing opinions and binding decisions, and promoting cooperation, training and information exchange among supervisory authorities.
Where the Commission requests advice from the Board, it may specify a time limit, taking into account the urgency of the matter.
The Board shall forward its opinions, guidelines, recommendations and best practices to the Commission and the committee referred to in Article 93 and shall make them publicly available.

Where appropriate, the Board shall consult interested parties and allow them a reasonable period to comment. Without prejudice to Article 76, it shall make the results of the consultation procedure publicly available.

The Board shall prepare an annual report on the protection of natural persons in relation to processing in the Union and, where relevant, in third countries and international organisations. The report shall be made public and transmitted to the European Parliament, the Council and the Commission.

The annual report shall review the practical application of the guidelines, recommendations and best practices referred to in Article 70(1)(l), as well as the binding decisions referred to in Article 65.
The Board shall take decisions by a simple majority of its members unless this Regulation provides otherwise.
The Board shall adopt its rules of procedure by a two-thirds majority of its members and shall organise its own operational arrangements.
The Board shall elect a Chair and two deputy chairs from among its members by simple majority.
The Chair and deputy chairs shall serve a five-year term of office, which may be renewed once.

The Chair shall convene Board meetings and prepare their agenda, notify decisions adopted under Article 65 to the lead and concerned supervisory authorities, and ensure the timely performance of the Board's tasks, particularly those relating to the consistency mechanism under Article 63.
The Board shall determine the allocation of tasks between the Chair and the deputy chairs in its rules of procedure.
The Board shall have a secretariat provided by the European Data Protection Supervisor.
The secretariat shall perform its tasks exclusively under the instructions of the Chair of the Board.
Staff of the European Data Protection Supervisor assigned to Board tasks shall have separate reporting lines from staff performing tasks assigned to the European Data Protection Supervisor.

Where appropriate, the Board and the European Data Protection Supervisor shall establish and publish a Memorandum of Understanding implementing this Article and setting the terms of their cooperation for the relevant staff.
The secretariat shall provide the Board with analytical, administrative and logistical support.

The secretariat shall be responsible in particular for the Board's day-to-day business; communication among Board members, the Chair and the Commission; communication with other institutions and the public; electronic communications; translation of relevant information; preparation and follow-up of Board meetings; and preparation, drafting and publication of Board opinions, dispute-settlement decisions and other adopted texts.
The Board's discussions shall be confidential where the Board considers this necessary, in accordance with its rules of procedure.

Access to documents submitted to Board members, experts and representatives of third parties shall be governed by Regulation (EC) No 1049/2001 on public access to European Parliament, Council and Commission documents.

article_name: Right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority

sections.text: Every data subject has the right, without prejudice to other administrative or judicial remedies, to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority if the data subject considers that processing of personal data relating to them infringes this Regulation. The complaint may in particular be lodged in the Member State of the data subject's habitual residence, place of work or place of the alleged infringement.

The supervisory authority with which the complaint was lodged shall inform the complainant of the progress and outcome of the complaint, including the possibility of a judicial remedy under Article 78.

article_name: Right to an effective judicial remedy against a supervisory authority

sections.text: Every natural or legal person has the right to an effective judicial remedy against a legally binding decision of a supervisory authority concerning them, without prejudice to other administrative or non-judicial remedies.

Every data subject has the right to an effective judicial remedy where the competent supervisory authority under Articles 55 and 56 does not handle a complaint or fails to inform the data subject within three months about the progress or outcome of a complaint lodged under Article 77.
Proceedings against a supervisory authority shall be brought before the courts of the Member State where that supervisory authority is established.

Where proceedings challenge a supervisory authority decision that was preceded by an opinion or decision of the Board under the consistency mechanism, the supervisory authority shall forward that opinion or decision to the court.

article_name: Right to an effective judicial remedy against a controller or processor

sections.text: Every data subject has the right to an effective judicial remedy, without prejudice to available administrative or non-judicial remedies, including the right to complain to a supervisory authority under Article 77, where the data subject considers that their rights under this Regulation have been infringed through processing of their personal data in non-compliance with this Regulation.

Proceedings against a controller or processor shall be brought before the courts of the Member State where the controller or processor has an establishment. Alternatively, proceedings may be brought before the courts of the Member State where the data subject has their habitual residence, unless the controller or processor is a public authority of a Member State acting in the exercise of its public powers.

A data subject has the right to mandate a properly constituted not-for-profit body, organisation or association with public-interest objectives active in protecting data subjects' rights and freedoms regarding personal data to lodge complaints and exercise the rights under Articles 77, 78 and 79 on their behalf, and, where provided by Member State law, to exercise the right to receive compensation under Article 82.

Member States may provide that qualifying bodies, organisations or associations may, independently of a data subject's mandate, lodge complaints with the competent supervisory authority and exercise the rights under Articles 78 and 79 where they consider that processing has infringed a data subject's rights under this Regulation.

Where a competent court of a Member State is informed of proceedings in another Member State concerning the same subject matter and processing by the same controller or processor, it shall contact that court to confirm the existence of those proceedings.

Where proceedings concerning the same subject matter and processing by the same controller or processor are pending in another Member State, any competent court other than the court first seised may suspend its proceedings.

Where proceedings are pending at first instance, a court other than the court first seised may, on application by a party, decline jurisdiction if the court first seised has jurisdiction over the actions and its law permits their consolidation.

Any person who suffers material or non-material damage resulting from an infringement of this Regulation has the right to receive compensation from the controller or processor for the damage suffered.

A controller involved in processing is liable for damage caused by processing that infringes this Regulation. A processor is liable only where it has failed to comply with obligations specifically directed to processors or has acted outside or contrary to lawful instructions of the controller.
A controller or processor is exempt from liability under paragraph 2 if it proves that it is not in any way responsible for the event giving rise to the damage.

Where multiple controllers or processors, or both controllers and processors, are involved in the same processing and are responsible for resulting damage under paragraphs 2 and 3, each shall be liable for the entire damage to ensure effective compensation of the data subject.

A controller or processor that has paid full compensation under paragraph 4 may claim from the other controllers or processors involved the portion of compensation corresponding to their responsibility for the damage, in accordance with paragraph 2.
Court proceedings to exercise the right to compensation shall be brought before the courts competent under the law of the Member State referred to in Article 79(2).

article_name: General conditions for imposing administrative fines

sections.text: Each supervisory authority shall ensure that administrative fines imposed for infringements referred to in paragraphs 4, 5 and 6 are effective, proportionate and dissuasive in each individual case.

Administrative fines may be imposed in addition to or instead of specified corrective measures under Article 58(2). The decision whether to impose a fine and its amount shall take account of the nature, gravity and duration of the infringement, its intentional or negligent character, mitigation measures, the controller's or processor's responsibility, previous infringements, cooperation, affected data categories, how the infringement became known, compliance with previous measures, adherence to approved codes or certification, and other aggravating or mitigating factors.

Where a controller or processor intentionally or negligently infringes several provisions of the Regulation through the same or linked processing operations, the total administrative fine shall not exceed the amount applicable to the gravest infringement.

Infringements of the obligations under Articles 8, 11, 25 to 39, 42 and 43, including specified obligations of certification and monitoring bodies, may be subject to fines of up to EUR 10 million or, for an undertaking, up to 2% of its total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher.

Infringements concerning the basic processing principles and consent conditions, data subject rights, international transfers, obligations under Member State law adopted pursuant to Chapter IX, or specified supervisory-authority measures and access requirements may be subject to fines of up to EUR 20 million or, for an undertaking, up to 4% of its total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher.

Non-compliance with an order issued by a supervisory authority under Article 58(2) may be subject to a fine of up to EUR 20 million or, for an undertaking, up to 4% of its total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher.

Without prejudice to the supervisory authorities' corrective powers under Article 58(2), each Member State may determine whether and to what extent administrative fines may be imposed on public authorities and bodies established in that Member State.

The exercise of supervisory-authority powers under this Article shall be subject to appropriate procedural safeguards under Union and Member State law, including effective judicial remedy and due process.

Where a Member State's legal system does not provide for administrative fines, this Article may be applied so that the competent supervisory authority initiates the fine and competent national courts impose it, with effective and equivalent legal remedies. Fines shall in all cases be effective, proportionate and dissuasive, and the Member State shall notify the Commission of the relevant legal provisions and subsequent amendments.

Member States shall establish rules on other penalties for infringements of this Regulation, particularly infringements not subject to administrative fines under Article 83, and shall take all necessary measures to ensure their implementation. Such penalties shall be effective, proportionate and dissuasive.
Each Member State shall notify the Commission of the legal provisions adopted under paragraph 1 by 25 May 2018 and, without delay, of any subsequent amendment affecting them.

article_name: Processing and freedom of expression and information

sections.text: Member States shall reconcile by law the right to protection of personal data under this Regulation with the right to freedom of expression and information, including processing for journalistic purposes and academic, artistic or literary expression.

For processing carried out for journalistic purposes or academic, artistic or literary expression, Member States shall provide necessary exemptions or derogations from specified provisions of Chapters II to VII and Chapter IX where required to reconcile data protection with freedom of expression and information.
Each Member State shall notify the Commission of the legal provisions adopted under paragraph 2 and, without delay, any subsequent amendment affecting them.

article_name: Processing and public access to official documents

sections.text: Personal data contained in official documents held by public authorities, public bodies, or private bodies performing a public-interest task may be disclosed in accordance with applicable Union or Member State law, in order to reconcile public access to official documents with the right to protection of personal data.

article_name: Processing of the national identification number

sections.text: Member States may further determine specific conditions for processing national identification numbers or other identifiers of general application. Where used, such identifiers must be subject to appropriate safeguards for the rights and freedoms of data subjects under the GDPR.

article_name: Processing in the context of employment

sections.text: Member States may establish, by law or collective agreements, more specific rules for processing employees' personal data in the employment context. Such rules must include suitable and specific measures safeguarding employees' dignity, legitimate interests and fundamental rights, particularly regarding transparency, intra-group transfers and workplace monitoring. Member States must notify the Commission of provisions adopted under this Article.

article_name: Safeguards and derogations relating to processing for archiving purposes in the public interest, scientific or historical research purposes or statistical purposes

sections.text: Processing for archiving in the public interest, scientific or historical research, or statistical purposes must be subject to appropriate safeguards protecting the rights and freedoms of data subjects. Technical and organisational measures must be used, particularly to ensure data minimisation. Pseudonymisation may be used where appropriate, and where the purposes can be achieved without identifying data subjects, processing should be carried out in that form.

For scientific or historical research or statistical purposes, Union or Member State law may provide derogations from Articles 15, 16, 18 and 21 where exercising those rights would likely make the purposes impossible or seriously impair their achievement, provided the derogations are necessary and the safeguards in paragraph 1 are applied.

For archiving purposes in the public interest, Union or Member State law may provide derogations from Articles 15, 16, 18, 19, 20 and 21 where exercising those rights would likely make the purposes impossible or seriously impair their achievement, provided the derogations are necessary and the safeguards in paragraph 1 are applied.
Where processing covered by paragraphs 2 or 3 also serves another purpose, the derogations apply only to the processing carried out for the specified archiving, research or statistical purposes.

Member States may adopt specific rules governing the supervisory authorities' investigative powers in relation to controllers or processors subject to professional secrecy or equivalent secrecy obligations, where necessary and proportionate to reconcile data protection with the obligation of secrecy. Such rules apply only to personal data covered by the secrecy obligation. Member States must notify the Commission of rules adopted under this Article.

article_name: Existing data protection rules of churches and religious associations

sections.text: Churches and religious associations or communities may continue to apply comprehensive data protection rules that existed when the Regulation entered into force, provided that those rules are brought into line with the GDPR.

Churches and religious associations applying comprehensive rules under paragraph 1 must be subject to supervision by an independent supervisory authority, which may be a specific authority if it satisfies the requirements of Chapter VI.
The Commission's power to adopt delegated acts is subject to the conditions laid down in Article 92.
The delegation of power concerning Articles 12(8) and 43(8) is conferred on the Commission for an indeterminate period from 24 May 2016.

The European Parliament or the Council may revoke the delegation of power at any time. A revocation terminates the specified delegation, takes effect as provided by its publication, and does not affect delegated acts already in force.
When adopting a delegated act, the Commission must notify the European Parliament and the Council simultaneously.

A delegated act under Articles 12(8) or 43(8) enters into force only if neither the European Parliament nor the Council objects within the specified period, subject to the possibility of extending that period by three months.
The Commission shall be assisted by a committee established in accordance with Regulation (EU) No 182/2011.
Where the GDPR refers to Article 93(2), the examination procedure under Article 5 of Regulation (EU) No 182/2011 shall apply.
Where the GDPR refers to Article 93(3), the procedure under Article 8 of Regulation (EU) No 182/2011, together with Article 5 of that Regulation, shall apply.
Directive 95/46/EC is repealed with effect from 25 May 2018.

References to the repealed Directive are to be construed as references to the GDPR. References to the Article 29 Working Party are to be construed as references to the European Data Protection Board established by the GDPR.

The GDPR does not impose additional obligations on natural or legal persons for processing connected with publicly available electronic communications services in public communication networks where they are already subject to specific obligations under Directive 2002/58/EC addressing the same objective.

International agreements concerning transfers of personal data to third countries or international organisations, concluded by Member States before 24 May 2016 and compliant with Union law applicable before that date, remain in force until they are amended, replaced or revoked.
By 25 May 2020 and every four years thereafter, the Commission shall submit a public report evaluating and reviewing the GDPR to the European Parliament and the Council.
As part of the evaluation and review, the Commission shall examine the application and functioning of Chapter V on international transfers and Chapter VII on cooperation and consistency.
For the evaluation and review, the Commission may request information from Member States and supervisory authorities.
In carrying out the evaluations and reviews, the Commission shall take into account the positions and findings of the European Parliament, the Council and other relevant bodies or sources.
Where necessary, the Commission shall submit appropriate proposals to amend the GDPR, taking account of developments in information technology and progress in the information society.

article_name: Review of other Union legal acts on data protection

sections.text: The Commission shall, if appropriate, submit legislative proposals to amend other Union legal acts concerning the protection of personal data, with the aim of ensuring uniform and consistent protection of natural persons. This particularly concerns rules governing processing by Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies and the free movement of personal data.
The GDPR enters into force on the twentieth day following its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union.
The GDPR applies from 25 May 2018.
